_README: Committed per-lab PERFORMANCE budget for the SHIPPED firmware users actually
boot. Enforced by crates/core/tests/esp32c3_shipped_lab_batch_gate.rs.
Each row is one shipped lab (see packages/playground/src/bundled-configs.ts).
The metric is MEAN BATCH WIDTH = cpu_instructions / cpu_batches, a pure
function of the model — bit-deterministic and machine-independent, NOT
wall-clock MIPS (which would flake on a loaded CI box). A collapsing batch
width IS the shipped-regression class this gate exists to catch (a per-cycle
scheduler wakeup pinning every batch to width ~1, dragging the browser far
below real time).
Fields per lab:
boot            - boot machinery required to run the binary. Only
'esp32c3-rom' rows are executed by the current gate; other
kinds SKIP cleanly with a note until their boot path is
wired (see the test module docs).
chip_yaml       - configs/chips/<chip>.yaml
system_yaml     - configs/systems/<system>.yaml
flash_basename  - shipped flash image under
packages/playground/public/wasm/ (NOT vendored into core).
min_mean_batch  - floor for mean batch width. Set well below the healthy
measured value and well above the collapse floor (1.0).
min_lit_px      - floor for lit OLED pixels: a fast engine that renders
nothing is not a pass.
min_idle_ff_ratio - floor for idle_fast_forward_cycles_skipped / total_cycles;
the browser fast-start policy must keep skipping idle time.
min_serial_bytes - liveness floor for rows with no readable display (the
classic-ESP32 e-paper row). Some non-zero liveness floor
is MANDATORY on every row: the fastest configurations ever
measured on classic ESP32 were fast BECAUSE they were
wedged and emitted nothing.
max_legacy_ticks_per_cycle - CEILING on legacy_tick_entries / total_cycles.
0 or absent disables it.
WHY TWO METRICS, NOT ONE
Mean batch width catches the batch-COLLAPSE class that took down the C3 labs.
It does NOT catch classic-ESP32 slowness. Measured on the shipped e-reader:
batch width 108.9 — which reads as perfectly healthy — while that same
configuration runs ~7x below what the engine can do. The cost on that chip is
per-cycle peripheral walk work, which batch width cannot see. So classic rows
also carry a walk-work ceiling. A batch-width floor alone would have been
decorative on the very chip whose regression prompted this row.
WHAT THIS ROW DOES AND DOES NOT DO
max_legacy_ticks_per_cycle stops classic ESP32 getting SLOWER. It does not
make it fast — 0.165 measured today IS the slow state, and the fix is raising
the tick interval above 1 (blocked on max_safe_tick_interval in bus/policy.rs
gating interval>1 on walk deletion). When that lands, TIGHTEN this ceiling in
the same PR to lock the win in; otherwise the gate quietly permits sliding
back.
Raising a floor tightens the gate (good). Lowering one is a deliberate act:
re-measure, explain, and move it in the same PR that changes the firmware.
